options.text: A project documentation file for developers
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md is intended for an AI agent, not for developers. Although people can also read it, its main purpose is instructions for Claude Code

options.text: A Markdown file with instructions for an AI agent, loaded automatically when Claude Code starts
options.explanation: Correct! CLAUDE.md is an 'onboarding document' for the agent that determines how the agent will work with your project

options.text: A configuration file in JSON format
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md is a Markdown file, not JSON. It's written in regular Markdown with headings and lists

options.text: A log file where Claude Code records its actions
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md is an instruction file that you write yourself. The agent reads it, not writes to it

question: Where should a project-level CLAUDE.md be located?

options.text: In the project root: ./CLAUDE.md
options.explanation: One of two standard locations for project-level CLAUDE.md

options.text: In the .claude directory: ./.claude/CLAUDE.md
options.explanation: The second standard option -- convenient to keep the project root clean

options.text: In the home directory: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
options.explanation: This is user-level CLAUDE.md, which applies to all projects, not a specific one

options.text: In the node_modules directory
options.explanation: node_modules is the dependencies directory, CLAUDE.md should not be placed there

question: What information should NOT be in CLAUDE.md?

options.text: Commands for running tests
options.explanation: Build and test commands are one of the most important parts of CLAUDE.md. Without them, the agent will guess

options.text: Information the agent can infer from project configuration (tsconfig.json, package.json)
options.explanation: Correct! Writing 'the project is in TypeScript' when tsconfig.json exists wastes tokens. Describe only what cannot be inferred from files

options.text: Architectural decisions and constraints
options.explanation: Architectural decisions (why Zustand, not Redux) are valuable information that the agent cannot learn from code

options.text: Gotchas and pitfalls
options.explanation: Gotchas are the most valuable part of CLAUDE.md. These are things that cannot be learned from code

question: Why should CLAUDE.md not be longer than 200 lines?

options.text: Claude Code cannot read long files
options.explanation: Claude Code can read files of any length. The limitation is not technical

options.text: It loads entirely into the context window, taking space away from code and conversation
options.explanation: Correct! Every line of CLAUDE.md is tokens from the context window. The longer the file, the less room for your code, command results, and conversation

options.text: Markdown does not support files longer than 200 lines
options.explanation: Markdown has no file length restrictions. This is a recommendation for efficient context usage

options.text: A long file slows down Claude Code startup
options.explanation: CLAUDE.md length does not affect startup speed. The problem is context window consumption

question: What does the @path construct do in CLAUDE.md?

options.text: Creates a symbolic link to a file
options.explanation: @path does not create filesystem links. It is a content import directive

options.text: Imports the contents of the specified file into the agent's context
options.explanation: Correct! @path allows you to decompose instructions: the root CLAUDE.md stays concise, while details are loaded from separate files

options.text: Prohibits agent access to the specified file
options.explanation: @path imports a file, it does not prohibit access to it. Other mechanisms are used for constraints

options.text: Adds the file to .gitignore
options.explanation: @path is a Claude Code directive, it does not affect git

question: What is the maximum @path import depth?

options.text: No limit
options.explanation: There is a limit to prevent cyclic imports and excessive context consumption

options.text: 3 levels
options.explanation: The limit is higher -- up to 5 levels of nesting are allowed

options.text: 5 levels
options.explanation: Correct! File A can import B, B can import C, and so on up to 5 levels deep

options.text: 10 levels
options.explanation: The maximum depth is 5 levels, which is sufficient for any reasonable structure

options.text: Initializes a new project from scratch
options.explanation: /init does not create a project -- it analyzes an existing project and creates CLAUDE.md

options.text: Analyzes the project (package.json, tsconfig, structure) and generates an initial CLAUDE.md
options.explanation: Correct! /init examines the project configuration and creates a basic CLAUDE.md that you then extend

options.text: Resets CLAUDE.md to default values
options.explanation: /init creates a new CLAUDE.md based on project analysis, not a reset to some 'default values'

options.text: Installs Claude Code into the project
options.explanation: Claude Code is installed globally via npm, and /init is a command within an already-running Claude Code session

question: What is user-level CLAUDE.md (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) used for?

options.text: For specific project settings
options.explanation: Specific project settings go in project-level CLAUDE.md (./CLAUDE.md). User-level is for personal preferences

options.text: For personal preferences that apply to all projects
options.explanation: Correct! Things like 'respond in English', 'use Conventional Commits' -- settings not tied to a specific project go here

options.text: For storing API keys
options.explanation: Never store secrets in CLAUDE.md! Use environment variables for keys

options.text: For instructions that cannot be overridden
options.explanation: Non-overrideable instructions are managed policy (corporate level), not user-level

question: You see this line in CLAUDE.md: 'The project uses TypeScript'. There is a tsconfig.json in the project root. What's wrong?

options.text: Nothing, this is useful information
options.explanation: The agent will discover tsconfig.json and understand the project is in TypeScript. This line duplicates the obvious

options.text: This is duplication -- the agent will detect TypeScript from tsconfig.json, the line wastes tokens
options.explanation: Correct! The agent analyzes configuration files. Describe only what cannot be inferred: non-obvious conventions, constraints, gotchas

options.text: Should be replaced with 'The project uses TypeScript strict mode'
options.explanation: Strict mode is also visible from tsconfig.json. Better to describe non-obvious TypeScript conventions, e.g.: 'use as const instead of enum'

options.text: Should add a link to tsconfig.json
options.explanation: The agent will find tsconfig.json itself. A link to it is another line wasting context

question: How should you properly structure instructions for a large project with many conventions?

options.text: Everything in one CLAUDE.md, so it's all in one place
options.explanation: This results in a file of hundreds of lines that eats up a significant portion of the context window

options.text: Compact root CLAUDE.md (50-100 lines) + decomposition via @path
options.explanation: Correct! The root file contains the most important info, while details are in separate files via @path. This saves context while preserving instruction completeness

options.text: Multiple CLAUDE.md files in the root with different names
options.explanation: Claude Code looks only for a file named CLAUDE.md. Files with other names will not be automatically loaded

options.text: Don't use CLAUDE.md, describe everything in conversation
options.explanation: Without CLAUDE.md, you'll have to repeat instructions every session, wasting context and time

question: In what order do CLAUDE.md scopes apply?

options.text: Only one scope is active -- the one closest to the file
options.explanation: All scopes merge, they do not replace each other. Instructions from all levels are active simultaneously

options.text: Managed Policy -> User -> Project -> Subdirectory (all merge together)
options.explanation: Correct! All scopes merge. Managed Policy has the highest priority and cannot be overridden. Other levels complement each other

options.text: Subdirectory overrides Project, Project overrides User
options.explanation: Scopes do not override, they complement each other. Instructions from all levels are active simultaneously

options.text: Order is random, depends on the session
options.explanation: The order is fixed and predictable: Managed Policy -> User -> Project -> Subdirectory

question: Your CLAUDE.md contains the line: 'Use React Router v5'. But the project has already migrated to v7. What will this lead to?

options.text: The agent will ignore the outdated instruction
options.explanation: The agent trusts CLAUDE.md and will follow the instruction. It may use deprecated v5 APIs instead of the new v7 APIs

options.text: The agent will generate code with deprecated v5 APIs, which may lead to errors
options.explanation: Correct! The agent doesn't know the instruction is outdated. It will write code with Switch, Route from v5 instead of new v7 constructs. Update CLAUDE.md regularly!

options.text: Claude Code will warn about a mismatch
options.explanation: Claude Code does not automatically check CLAUDE.md instruction relevance. This is your responsibility

options.text: Nothing bad, the agent will determine the version itself
options.explanation: The agent may determine the version from package.json, but an explicit instruction in CLAUDE.md takes priority, and the agent will follow it

question: Which of the following gotchas should be described in CLAUDE.md?

options.text: CI fails if you forget pnpm run generate after changing the GraphQL schema
options.explanation: This cannot be learned from code. The agent may change the schema and not run codegen -- a perfect candidate for CLAUDE.md

options.text: TypeScript requires typing
options.explanation: This is basic knowledge about TypeScript, not project-specific

options.text: auth module tests must be run sequentially (--runInBand)
options.explanation: A non-obvious feature of a specific module. Without this information, the agent will run tests in parallel and they will fail

options.text: npm install installs dependencies
options.explanation: This is common knowledge, not related to project specifics

options.text: Environment variables go in .env.local, not .env
options.explanation: A project-specific convention. By default, the agent may create .env, which will not work
